title.narrative: Scaling Sustainable Livelihoods and Environmental Renewal through Eco-Briquettes (SSLEREB)

description.narrative: The project seeks to address the pressing challenges of environmental degradation, high household fuel costs, and limited economic opportunities for vulnerable women and youth, through the production of eco-friendly briquettes using solar-powered machinery. This initiative aims to reduce reliance on traditional charcoal, mitigate deforestation, and promote sustainable energy solutions. The adoption of eco-friendly briquettes and energy-saving cooking stoves has contributed to environmental conservation efforts, including the planting of 1,000 economic trees and extensive awareness campaigns against deforestation. Notably, a good number of priests in Abuja and Kaduna State now utilize briquette charcoal during Mass, reflecting a growing shift towards sustainable fuel alternatives. Carbonized briquettes can act as a replacement for charcoal for domestic and institutional cooking and heating, where they are favored for their near-smokeless use. In comparison to charcoal, they generally burn for longer and have a more consistent heat output, which is preferred by certain market segments such as restaurants, hospitals, schools, and poultry farmers. The use of briquettes for cooking will drastically reduce the demand for firewood in the community because of its low costs, efficiency, and effectiveness.
